method: Manual source and candidate-office review of cached rendered text. Raw captures remain outside Git. Source labels and factual match fields are retained; summaries are paraphrases. No model grading and no automatic endorsement inference from Sources badges.

vote_for_peace.publisher: Vote for Peace / Organize For Peace

track_aipac.publisher: Track AIPAC / Citizens Against AIPAC Corruption
track_aipac.review: Connie Chan, Lateefah Simon and Ro Khanna independently confirmed for the general election. Their existing first-party records are preserved without duplicates. No Track AIPAC opposition is inferred from funding data or its absence from this endorsement list.

jane_kim_campaign.review: For the People Action explicitly appears in Organizations. Broader campaign-list expansion is outside this targeted source integration.

notes.N296: Vote for Peace / Organize For Peace: source labels checked October 9, 2026. Ally is the guide’s own alignment label, not a formal endorsement; its methodology distinguishes inclusion from endorsement. Opposed is the guide’s negative recommendation. Neutral is not imported as support or opposition. Election phase follows the California list, including Jimmy Panetta’s primary entry. Other groups listed under Sources are research references, not automatically endorsers or opponents. https://voteforpeace.info/methodology
notes.N297: AROC Action’s official page explicitly identifies its candidate endorsements as for November 3, 2026. Names and offices were matched to the current printed roster on October 9. Multiple names in one contest are retained without inventing a rank or an explicit joint-endorsement designation. Ballot measures and candidates outside the current roster are preserved in the source review manifest.
notes.N298: Vote for Peace explicitly reports this organizational endorsement in Malia Cohen’s candidate notes. This is a secondary report associated with its 2026 general-election listing, not independent confirmation from the named organization. https://voteforpeace.info/california/malia-cohen
notes.N299: Working Families Party announced its endorsement of Jane Kim for California Insurance Commissioner on January 21, 2026. The announcement does not specify primary versus general-election scope, so phase remains unspecified. Discovered through Vote for Peace and verified on the party’s own site.
notes.N300: For the People Action appears in the Organizations section of Jane Kim’s current Insurance Commissioner endorsement page. This is a campaign claim, independently located through a Vote for Peace source reference; election phase is not explicitly stated on that endorsement list.
